verses.1: Working together, then, we appeal to you not to receive the grace of God in vain.
verses.2: For he says: "In an acceptable time I heard you, and on the day of salvation I helped you." Behold, now is a very acceptable time; behold, now is the day of salvation.
verses.3: We cause no one to stumble in anything, in order that no fault may be found with our ministry;
verses.4: on the contrary, in everything we commend ourselves as ministers of God, through much endurance, in afflictions, hardships, constraints,
verses.5: beatings, imprisonments, riots, labors, vigils, fasts;
verses.6: by purity, knowledge, patience, kindness, in a holy spirit, in unfeigned love,
verses.7: in truthful speech, in the power of God; with weapons of righteousness at the right and at the left;
verses.8: through glory and dishonor, insult and praise. We are treated as deceivers and yet are truthful;
verses.9: as unrecognized and yet acknowledged; as dying and behold we live; as chastised and yet not put to death;
verses.10: as sorrowful yet always rejoicing; as poor yet enriching many; as having nothing and yet possessing all things.
verses.11: We have spoken frankly to you, Corinthians; our heart is open wide.
verses.12: You are not constrained by us; you are constrained by your own affections.
verses.13: As recompense in kind (I speak as to my children), be open yourselves.
verses.14: Do not be yoked with those who are different, with unbelievers. For what partnership do righteousness and lawlessness have? Or what fellowship does light have with darkness?
verses.15: What accord has Christ with Beliar? Or what has a believer in common with an unbeliever?
verses.16: What agreement has the temple of God with idols? For we are the temple of the living God; as God said: "I will live with them and move among them, and I will be their God and they shall be my people.
verses.17: Therefore, come forth from them and be separate," says the Lord, "and touch nothing unclean; then I will receive you
verses.18: and I will be a father to you, and you shall be sons and daughters to me, says the Lord Almighty."

notes.text: This paragraph is a single long sentence in the Greek, interrupted by the parenthesis of 2 Cor 5:2. The one main verb is "we appeal." In this paragraph Paul both exercises his ministry of reconciliation (cf 2 Cor 5:20) and describes how his ministry is exercised: the "message of reconciliation" (2 Cor 5:19) is lived existentially in his apostolic experience.

Not to receive... in vain: i.e., conform to the gift of justification and new creation. The context indicates how this can be done concretely: become God's righteousness (2 Cor 5:21), not live for oneself (2 Cor 5:15) be reconciled with Paul (2 Cor 6:11-13; 7:2-3).

In an acceptable time: Paul cites the Septuagint text of Isaiah 49:8; the Hebrew reads "in a time of favor"; it is parallel to "on the day of salvation." Now: God is bestowing favor and salvation at this very moment, as Paul is addressing his letter to them.

Cause no one to stumble: the language echoes that of 1 Cor 8-10 as does the expression "no longer live for themselves" in 2 Cor 5:15. That no fault may be found: i.e., at the eschatological judgment (cf 1 Cor 4:2-5).

This is the central assertion, the topic statement for the catalogue that follows. We commend ourselves: Paul's self-commendation is ironical (with an eye on the charges mentioned in 2 Cor 3:1-3) and paradoxical (pointing mostly to experiences that would not normally be considered points of pride but are perceived as such by faith). Cf also the self-commendation in 2 Cor 11:23-29. As ministers of God: the same Greek word, diakonos, means "minister" and "servant"; cf 2 Cor 11:23, the central assertion in a similar context, and 1 Cor 3:5.
A list of virtuous qualities in two groups of four, the second fuller than the first.

Paul's tone becomes quieter, but his appeal for acceptance and affection is emotionally charged. References to the heart and their mutual relations bring the development begun in 2 Cor 2:14- 3:3 to an effective conclusion.

The opening injunction to separate from unbelievers is reinforced by five rhetorical questions to make the point that Christianity is not compatible with paganism. Their opposition is emphasized also by the accumulation of five distinct designations for each group. These verses are a powerful statement of God's holiness and the exclusiveness of his claims.
